findings.reason: the worker has to choose one of two contradictory rules on `handle`, and whichever it picks contradicts a sentence in the plan it is implementing.
findings.text: §6's Deliverable says a host "starts or restarts a child only when its entry carries `owner_checked: true` ... or when its session is the owner's current session", which covers the spawn `SessionHost.handle` (`reckon/crew/session_host.py:523-531`) makes for a request line; but §5 says the host "then serves its FIFO as today" and "A first request, when one is given, is served as today", and §5's own Why documents nova-4a writing `{"project":"nova","session":"<id>", ...}` to the FIFO by hand — a line that carries no mark and, for an earlier session of the same owner or any other session, is not the owner's current session. Two sections therefore give opposite instructions for the same path, and a §6 worker following its Deliverable silently disables the operator's documented re-arm motion that §5 says still works

findings.reason: adding the one sentence the sibling sections carry makes the §6 gate readable and its lint obligation explicit, which the node's promotion depends on.
findings.text: §6's done-when names "the gate log" and "Negative controls, each logged" but omits the convention §2-§5 all state: every log under the run directory, starting with its revision and the literal command, ending in a bare `EXIT=` line, plus "Ruff adds no findings on the staged paths" — promotion reads the exit status from that `EXIT=` line and a log without it leaves the §6 gate unreadable

findings.reason: the case still fails at the base revision on its other two assertions, so the redundant one costs a sentence, not a mechanism.
findings.text: §6's first case asserts the dropped child "is absent from the next `session-hosts` record", but `SessionHost.record()` (`reckon/crew/session_host.py:451-461`) already filters to children with a non-null pid or a settled marker, so a child that merely is not restarted (pid None, not settled) is absent at the base revision too; only the "not restarted" and "drop logged" assertions discriminate, and the case's discriminating power rests on them alone

response_events.note: section 6's rule now governs restarts only: a request line served by SessionHost.handle, including a hand-written one, starts its child as section 5 says, and only the restart of an exited unmarked child for another session is dropped
